fr: J'ai acheté du pain à la boulangerie ce matin.
en: I bought bread at the bakery this morning.
ipa: /ʒe a.ʃə.te dy pɛ̃ a la bu.lɑ̃ʒ.ʁi sə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: The preposition à and the verb form a sound identical, but only à fits before la boulangerie.

fr: Nous sommes allés au supermarché hier soir.
en: We went to the supermarket last night.
ipa: /nu sɔm a.le o sy.pɛʁ.maʁ.ʃe jɛʁ swaʁ/
notes: With être, the past participle allés must agree with the plural subject nous, adding a silent s.

fr: Elle a acheté deux kilos de pommes.
en: She bought two kilos of apples.
ipa: /ɛl a a.ʃə.te dø ki.lo də pɔm/
notes: The final x in deux is silent, so listeners must not add it when spelling the word.

fr: Ils ont trouvé la pharmacie fermée.
en: They found the pharmacy closed.
ipa: /il ɔ̃ tʁu.ve la faʁ.ma.si fɛʁ.me/
notes: Ont sounds exactly like on, so the subject ils tells you which spelling is correct.

fr: On a fait la queue pendant vingt minutes à la poste.
en: We waited in line for twenty minutes at the post office.
ipa: /ɔ̃.n‿a fɛ la kø pɑ̃.dɑ̃ vɛ̃ mi.nyt a la pɔst/
notes: Vingt ends in a nasal vowel with no audible consonant, which can make learners forget the silent g and t.

fr: Le magasin ferme à dix-neuf heures ce soir.
en: The store closes at seven p.m. tonight.
ipa: /lə ma.ga.zɛ̃ fɛʁm a diz.nœ.v‿œʁ sə swaʁ/
notes: The f of neuf becomes a v sound before heures because of liaison, which can confuse the spelling.

fr: J'ai oublié ma liste de courses à la maison.
en: I forgot my shopping list at home.
ipa: /ʒe u.bli.je ma list də kuʁs a la mɛ.zɔ̃/
notes: Je ai contracts to j'ai before a vowel, so the apostrophe must replace the dropped e.

fr: Nous allons acheter du fromage et des œufs.
en: We are going to buy cheese and eggs.
ipa: /nu.z‿a.lɔ̃ a.ʃə.te dy fʁɔ.maʒ e de.z‿ø/
notes: The s of des links to the vowel of œufs as a z sound, a liaison easy to miss in fast speech.

fr: Elle va rendre ce pull parce qu'il est trop petit.
en: She's going to return this sweater because it's too small.
ipa: /ɛl va ʁɑ̃dʁ sə pyl paʁ.skil ɛ tʁo pə.ti/
notes: Parce que drops its e before il, becoming parce qu'il in writing.

fr: Les clients ont attendu longtemps à la caisse.
en: The customers waited a long time at the checkout.
ipa: /le kli.jɑ̃ ɔ̃.t‿a.tɑ̃.dy lɔ̃.tɑ̃ a la kɛs/
notes: Ont is easy to confuse with on by sound alone, only the plural subject les clients confirms the spelling.

fr: Je vais demander un ticket de caisse pour l'échange.
en: I'm going to ask for a receipt for the exchange.
ipa: /ʒə vɛ də.mɑ̃.de ɛ̃ ti.kɛ də kɛs puʁ le.ʃɑ̃ʒ/
notes: The unstressed e in je is a schwa that can vanish in speech but must stay in spelling.

fr: Le boulanger a vendu tous les croissants avant midi.
en: The baker sold all the croissants before noon.
ipa: /lə bu.lɑ̃.ʒe a vɑ̃.dy tu le kʁwa.sɑ̃ a.vɑ̃ mi.di/
notes: Tous is pronounced without the final s here because it comes before a noun, unlike when used alone as a pronoun.

fr: On a payé la facture avec la carte bancaire.
en: We paid the bill with the bank card.
ipa: /ɔ̃.n‿a pe.je la fak.tyʁ a.vɛk la kaʁt bɑ̃.kɛʁ/
notes: On a can sound like on n'a in negative sentences, so listen for context to spell it correctly.

fr: Où as-tu mis le reçu du magasin ?
en: Where did you put the store receipt?
ipa: /u a ty mi lə ʁə.sy dy ma.ga.zɛ̃/
notes: Où (where) and ou (or) sound identical, only the accent distinguishes them in writing.

fr: Elle a rangé les courses dans le sac.
en: She put the groceries away in the bag.
ipa: /ɛl a ʁɑ̃.ʒe le kuʁs dɑ̃ lə sak/
notes: Because the direct object les courses comes after the verb, the past participle rangé stays unchanged despite the plural noun.

fr: Nous avons dépensé plus que prévu ce mois-ci.
en: We spent more than planned this month.
ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ de.pɑ̃.se plys kə pʁe.vy sə mwa.si/
notes: The final s in mois is silent, so it must not be added when writing the word.

fr: Ils vont ouvrir un nouveau magasin en ville.
en: They are going to open a new store in town.
ipa: /il vɔ̃ u.vʁiʁ ɛ̃ nu.vo ma.ga.zɛ̃ ɑ̃ vil/
notes: En is a nasal vowel with no audible n, so learners often forget the n when spelling it.

fr: J'ai pris rendez-vous chez le pharmacien à onze heures.
en: I made an appointment with the pharmacist at eleven o'clock.
ipa: /ʒe pʁi ʁɑ̃.de.vu ʃe lə faʁ.ma.sjɛ̃ a ɔ̃z œʁ/
notes: Onze contains a nasal vowel that is easy to mishear, which can make learners misspell the number.

fr: Le vendeur a compté la monnaie deux fois.
en: The salesman counted the change twice.
ipa: /lə vɑ̃.dœʁ a kɔ̃.te la mɔ.nɛ dø fwa/
notes: The past participle compté and the infinitive compter sound exactly the same, so grammar decides the correct ending.

fr: Nous avons acheté des fruits et des légumes frais.
en: We bought fruit and fresh vegetables.
ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ a.ʃə.te de fʁɥi e de le.gym fʁɛ/
notes: The final s in frais is silent, which can make learners drop or misplace it in writing.

fr: Elle est allée chercher un colis à la poste.
en: She went to pick up a parcel at the post office.
ipa: /ɛl ɛ.t‿a.le ʃɛʁ.ʃe ɛ̃ kɔ.li a la pɔst/
notes: With être, allée must agree with the feminine subject elle by adding a silent e.

fr: On va comparer les prix avant d'acheter.
en: We're going to compare prices before buying.
ipa: /ɔ̃ va kɔ̃.pa.ʁe le pʁi a.vɑ̃ da.ʃə.te/
notes: Avant de loses its e before a vowel, becoming avant d'acheter in writing.

fr: Les enfants ont choisi des bonbons à la caisse.
en: The children chose candy at the checkout.
ipa: /le.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ ɔ̃ ʃwa.zi de bɔ̃.bɔ̃ a la kɛs/
notes: Ont and on sound identical, so only the plural subject les enfants shows which spelling is right.

fr: J'ai payé en espèces parce que la carte ne marchait pas.
en: I paid in cash because the card wasn't working.
ipa: /ʒe pe.je ɑ̃.n‿ɛs.pɛs paʁs.kə la kaʁt nə maʁ.ʃɛ pa/
notes: The nasal vowel in en has no audible n by itself, which can cause learners to misspell it as an or drop a letter.

fr: Le magasin est ouvert du lundi au samedi.
en: The store is open from Monday to Saturday.
ipa: /lə ma.ga.zɛ̃ ɛ.t‿u.vɛʁ dy lœ̃.di o sam.di/
notes: Lundi begins with a nasal vowel that has no audible n, easy to misspell by ear.

fr: Nous avons attendu notre tour devant la boulangerie.
en: We waited our turn in front of the bakery.
ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃.z‿a.tɑ̃.dy nɔtʁ tuʁ də.vɑ̃ la bu.lɑ̃ʒ.ʁi/
notes: Nous avons links with a z sound before the vowel, a liaison that is easy to leave out in writing.

fr: Elle a acheté trois baguettes pour la semaine.
en: She bought three baguettes for the week.
ipa: /ɛl a a.ʃə.te tʁwa ba.gɛt puʁ la sə.mɛn/
notes: The final s in trois is silent, so it should never be added to the following word by ear.

fr: Ils ont fermé le magasin plus tôt aujourd'hui.
en: They closed the store earlier today.
ipa: /il ɔ̃ fɛʁ.me lə ma.ga.zɛ̃ ply.to o.ʒuʁ.dɥi/
notes: Ont sounds identical to on, so the plural pronoun ils is the only clue for the correct spelling.

fr: J'ai gardé le ticket pour l'échange.
en: I kept the receipt for the exchange.
ipa: /ʒe gaʁ.de lə ti.kɛ puʁ le.ʃɑ̃ʒ/
notes: Le échange contracts to l'échange before a vowel, so the article's e is replaced by an apostrophe.

fr: On a trouvé une promotion sur les pâtes.
en: We found a promotion on pasta.
ipa: /ɔ̃.n‿a tʁu.ve yn pʁɔ.mɔ.sjɔ̃ syʁ le pɑt/
notes: On a can be mistaken for on n'a in fast speech, so context tells you whether to add n'.

fr: Le facteur a apporté un paquet ce matin.
en: The mailman brought a package this morning.
ipa: /lə fak.tœʁ a a.pɔʁ.te ɛ̃ pa.kɛ sə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: The unstressed e in le is a schwa that weakens in speech but must still be written.

fr: Nous avons fait la liste avant d'aller au marché.
en: We made the list before going to the market.
ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ fɛ la list a.vɑ̃ da.le o maʁ.ʃe/
notes: Avant de elides its e before the vowel of aller, becoming avant d'aller in writing.

fr: Elle va acheter un cadeau pour sa mère.
en: She's going to buy a gift for her mother.
ipa: /ɛl va a.ʃə.te ɛ̃ ka.do puʁ sa mɛʁ/
notes: The possessive sa and the pronoun ça sound alike, so only meaning shows which one to write.

fr: Les prix ont beaucoup augmenté cette année.
en: Prices have gone up a lot this year.
ipa: /le pʁi ɔ̃ bo.ku og.mɑ̃.te sɛ.t‿a.ne/
notes: Cette links to année with a liaison t sound that is easy to miss when spelling the phrase.

fr: J'ai oublié où j'ai garé la voiture au parking du centre commercial.
en: I forgot where I parked the car at the mall parking lot.
ipa: /ʒe u.bli.je u ʒe ga.ʁe la vwa.tyʁ o paʁ.kiŋ dy sɑ̃tʁ kɔ.mɛʁ.sjal/
notes: Où (where) and ou (or) are perfect homophones, distinguished only by the accent.

fr: On a demandé un sac réutilisable à la caisse.
en: We asked for a reusable bag at the checkout.
ipa: /ɔ̃.n‿a də.mɑ̃.de ɛ̃ sak ʁe.y.ti.li.zabl a la kɛs/
notes: On a and on n'a sound the same without context, so listen for the full sentence meaning.

fr: Ils ont livré la commande en retard.
en: They delivered the order late.
ipa: /il ɔ̃ liv.ʁe la kɔ.mɑ̃d ɑ̃ ʁə.taʁ/
notes: En retard contains a nasal vowel with no audible n, a common spelling trap by ear.

fr: Nous allons faire les courses ensemble ce week-end.
en: We're going to do the shopping together this weekend.
ipa: /nu.z‿a.lɔ̃ fɛʁ le kuʁs ɑ̃.sɑ̃bl sə wik.ɛnd/
notes: Ensemble has two nasal vowels in a row, which can make learners drop a syllable when spelling it.

fr: Elle a vérifié le prix avant de payer.
en: She checked the price before paying.
ipa: /ɛl a ve.ʁi.fje lə pʁi a.vɑ̃ də pe.je/
notes: Vérifié and vérifier sound identical, so only the grammar shows which ending is correct.

fr: Il faut que tu ailles à la pharmacie avant qu'elle ne ferme.
en: You need to go to the pharmacy before it closes.
ipa: /il fo kə ty aj a la faʁ.ma.si a.vɑ̃ kɛl nə fɛʁm/
notes: The subjunctive ailles ends in a silent s that is not heard, easy to omit when writing.

fr: Je pense que ces produits sont trop chers pour notre budget.
en: I think these products are too expensive for our budget.
ipa: /ʒə pɑ̃s kə se pʁɔ.dɥi sɔ̃ tʁo ʃɛʁ puʁ nɔtʁ by.dʒɛ/
notes: Ces (these) sounds exactly like ses (his/her) and c'est (it is), so only context tells you which to write.

fr: Quelle boulangerie recommandes-tu dans ce quartier ?
en: Which bakery do you recommend in this neighborhood?
ipa: /kɛl bu.lɑ̃ʒ.ʁi ʁə.kɔ.mɑ̃d ty dɑ̃ sə kaʁ.tje/
notes: Quelle and quel sound identical, so the feminine noun boulangerie tells you which spelling fits.

fr: Il est possible que le magasin soit fermé le dimanche.
en: It's possible that the store is closed on Sundays.
ipa: /il ɛ pɔ.sibl kə lə ma.ga.zɛ̃ swa fɛʁ.me lə di.mɑ̃ʃ/
notes: The subjunctive soit sounds exactly like soi and soie, so grammar alone decides the spelling.

fr: Ces chaussures que j'ai achetées ne me vont pas du tout.
en: These shoes that I bought don't suit me at all.
ipa: /se ʃo.syʁ kə ʒe a.ʃə.te nə mə vɔ̃ pa dy tu/
notes: Because the direct object que refers back to chaussures, achetées must agree in the feminine plural.

fr: C'est ce vendeur qui m'a conseillé cette marque de café.
en: It's this salesman who recommended this brand of coffee to me.
ipa: /sɛ sə vɑ̃.dœʁ ki ma kɔ̃.sɛ.je sɛt maʁk də ka.fe/
notes: C'est and ces are perfect homophones, only sentence structure shows which one belongs here.

fr: Bien que les prix aient augmenté, je continue d'y faire mes courses.
en: Although prices have gone up, I keep shopping there.
ipa: /bjɛ̃ kə le pʁi ɛ og.mɑ̃.te ʒə kɔ̃.ti.ny di fɛʁ me kuʁs/
notes: The subjunctive aient is pronounced just like ai, es, est and aie, so only grammar shows the right form.

fr: Je doute que ce magasin accepte les retours sans ticket.
en: I doubt this store accepts returns without a receipt.
ipa: /ʒə dut kə sə ma.ga.zɛ̃ ak.sɛpt le ʁə.tuʁ sɑ̃ ti.kɛ/
notes: For -er verbs, the subjunctive accepte sounds identical to the indicative form, so context signals the mood.

fr: Il faudrait que nous fassions la liste avant de partir.
en: We should make the list before leaving.
ipa: /il fo.dʁɛ kə nu fa.sjɔ̃ la list a.vɑ̃ də paʁ.tiʁ/
notes: Fassions contains a nasal vowel that can lead learners to misspell the subjunctive ending of faire.

fr: Ses économies lui permettent de comparer les prix sans stress.
en: Her savings allow her to compare prices without stress.
ipa: /se.z‿e.kɔ.nɔ.mi lɥi pɛʁ.mɛt də kɔ̃.pa.ʁe le pʁi sɑ̃ stʁɛs/
notes: Ses sounds identical to ces and c'est, so only the possessive meaning confirms the spelling.

fr: Ce sont les soldes qui attirent le plus de clients en janvier.
en: It's the sales that attract the most customers in January.
ipa: /sə sɔ̃ le sɔld ki a.tiʁ lə plys də kli.jɑ̃ ɑ̃ ʒɑ̃.vje/
notes: Ce sont (it is/these are) sounds like se sont, so only the impersonal meaning shows which to write.

fr: Je ne pense pas que cette réduction soit encore valable.
en: I don't think this discount is still valid.
ipa: /ʒə nə pɑ̃s pa kə sɛt ʁe.dyk.sjɔ̃ swa.t‿ɑ̃.kɔʁ va.labl/
notes: The subjunctive soit links to encore with a t sound, a liaison that is easy to leave out in writing.

fr: Quel est le prix de ce paquet de café moulu ?
en: What is the price of this bag of ground coffee?
ipa: /kɛl ɛ lə pʁi də sə pa.kɛ də ka.fe mu.ly/
notes: Ce (this) and se (reflexive pronoun) sound the same, so grammar shows which spelling is correct here.

fr: Se rendre au marché tôt permet d'éviter la foule.
en: Going to the market early helps you avoid the crowd.
ipa: /sə ʁɑ̃dʁ o maʁ.ʃe to pɛʁ.mɛ de.vi.te la ful/
notes: The reflexive se and the demonstrative ce are pronounced identically, so only grammar tells them apart.

fr: C'est la caissière qui a signalé l'erreur sur le reçu.
en: It's the cashier who reported the error on the receipt.
ipa: /sɛ la kɛ.sjɛʁ ki a si.ɲa.le lɛ.ʁœʁ syʁ lə ʁə.sy/
notes: The past participle signalé and the infinitive signaler sound the same, so only grammar fixes the ending.

fr: Il semble que la pharmacie ait changé ses horaires d'ouverture.
en: It seems the pharmacy has changed its opening hours.
ipa: /il sɑ̃bl kə la faʁ.ma.si ɛ ʃɑ̃.ʒe se.z‿ɔ.ʁɛʁ du.vɛʁ.tyʁ/
notes: The subjunctive ait sounds like es, est, ai and aie, so only the clause structure confirms the spelling.

fr: Ces articles se vendent mieux depuis la promotion.
en: These items have been selling better since the promotion.
ipa: /se.z‿aʁ.tikl sə vɑ̃d mjø də.pɥi la pʁɔ.mɔ.sjɔ̃/
notes: Ces and se are pronounced the same way, so only their grammatical role shows which spelling to use.

fr: Je suis content que tu aies trouvé une bonne affaire.
en: I'm glad you found a good deal.
ipa: /ʒə sɥi kɔ̃.tɑ̃ kə ty ɛ tʁu.ve yn bɔn a.fɛʁ/
notes: The subjunctive aies sounds exactly like ait, es, est and ai, so grammar alone gives the spelling.

fr: Il vaut mieux que vous vérifiiez le prix avant de payer.
en: You'd better check the price before paying.
ipa: /il vo mjø kə vu ve.ʁi.fje lə pʁi a.vɑ̃ də pe.je/
notes: The subjunctive vérifiiez has an unusual double i that is barely audible, making it easy to misspell.

fr: Ce magasin propose des produits que je n'avais jamais vus ailleurs.
en: This store offers products that I had never seen elsewhere.
ipa: /sə ma.ga.zɛ̃ pʁɔ.poz de pʁɔ.dɥi kə ʒə na.vɛ ʒa.mɛ vy.z‿aj.œʁ/
notes: Because the preceding direct object que refers to produits, the past participle vus takes a plural s.

fr: Bien qu'elle soit pressée, elle a fait la queue sans se plaindre.
en: Although she was in a hurry, she waited in line without complaining.
ipa: /bjɛ̃ kɛl swa pʁɛ.se ɛl a fɛ la kø sɑ̃ sə plɛ̃dʁ/
notes: Que elle contracts to qu'elle before the vowel, so the apostrophe replaces the dropped e.

fr: Ses clients préfèrent que le magasin reste ouvert le soir.
en: Its customers prefer the store to stay open in the evening.
ipa: /se kli.jɑ̃ pʁe.fɛʁ kə lə ma.ga.zɛ̃ ʁɛst u.vɛʁ lə swaʁ/
notes: Ses sounds identical to ces and c'est, so only the possessive sense shows which spelling fits.

fr: C'est un colis que j'attends depuis une semaine à la poste.
en: It's a parcel that I've been waiting for at the post office for a week.
ipa: /sɛ.t‿ɛ̃ kɔ.li kə ʒa.tɑ̃ də.pɥi yn sə.mɛn a la pɔst/
notes: C'est links to un with a t sound, a liaison that is easy to forget when writing the phrase.

fr: Il faut qu'on prenne un numéro avant d'être servi.
en: You have to take a number before being served.
ipa: /il fo kɔ̃ pʁɛn ɛ̃ ny.me.ʁo a.vɑ̃ dɛtʁ sɛʁ.vi/
notes: Que on contracts to qu'on before the vowel, and d'être similarly drops the e of de.

fr: Quelles sont les conditions pour se faire rembourser ?
en: What are the conditions to get a refund?
ipa: /kɛl sɔ̃ le kɔ̃.di.sjɔ̃ puʁ sə fɛʁ ʁɑ̃.buʁ.se/
notes: Quelles sounds identical to quelle and quel, so the plural noun conditions shows the correct ending.

fr: Ce n'est pas parce que c'est en solde que c'est de bonne qualité.
en: It's not because it's on sale that it's good quality.
ipa: /sə nɛ pa paʁs.kə sɛ.t‿ɑ̃ sɔld kə sɛ də bɔn ka.li.te/
notes: Ce and c'est are easy to confuse by ear since both start with the same sound before the verb.

fr: Je crains que ce produit ne soit plus en stock aujourd'hui.
en: I'm afraid this product is no longer in stock today.
ipa: /ʒə kʁɛ̃ kə sə pʁɔ.dɥi nə swa ply.z‿ɑ̃ stɔk o.ʒuʁ.dɥi/
notes: En stock carries a nasal vowel with no audible n, a common spelling trap in dictation.

fr: Ces prix se comparent facilement grâce à l'application du magasin.
en: These prices are easy to compare thanks to the store's app.
ipa: /se pʁi sə kɔ̃.paʁ fa.sil.mɑ̃ gʁas a la.pli.ka.sjɔ̃ dy ma.ga.zɛ̃/
notes: Ces and se sound exactly alike, so only their grammatical function shows which spelling is right.

fr: Il est essentiel que vous gardiez votre ticket de caisse.
en: It's essential that you keep your receipt.
ipa: /il ɛ.t‿e.sɑ̃.sjɛl kə vu gaʁ.dje vɔtʁ ti.kɛ də kɛs/
notes: The subjunctive gardiez is spelled the same as the imperfect indicative form, so only the clause structure tells them apart.

fr: C'est en comparant les prix qu'on fait de vraies économies.
en: It's by comparing prices that you make real savings.
ipa: /sɛ.t‿ɑ̃ kɔ̃.pa.ʁɑ̃ le pʁi kɔ̃ fɛ də vʁɛ e.kɔ.nɔ.mi/
notes: Que on contracts to qu'on in writing, even though the full vowel sound almost disappears in speech.

fr: Se plaindre au service client a permis d'obtenir un remboursement.
en: Complaining to customer service made it possible to get a refund.
ipa: /sə plɛ̃dʁ o sɛʁ.vis kli.jɑ̃ a pɛʁ.mi dɔb.tə.niʁ ɛ̃ ʁɑ̃.buʁs.mɑ̃/
notes: De obtenir elides to d'obtenir before the vowel, so the apostrophe replaces the dropped e in writing.
